* * * *
 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 17.08.2022 at about 7.00 pm., when the petitioner was riding the Honda Sine vehicle bearing (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.5888/2022 reg.No.KA-06-EY-1138 from Huliyurdurga towards Kenkere village on the extreme left side on Maduur - Kunigal main SH - 33 road slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations and when petitioner reached near Kodavatti junction, Huliyurdurga Bypass road,
Kunigal taluk, Tumkur, at that time, suddenly, the driver of Canter bearing reg.No.KA-16-C- 5792 came from Maddur towards Kunigal side in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations in a zig zag manner and dashed against the petitioner's Honda Shine vehicle and caused the accident.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down along with the vehicle and sustained grevious injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Kunigal Government Hospital in a 108 Ambulance wherein after first aid treatment, petitioner was referred to Adichunchanagiri Hospital & Research (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.5888/2022 Centre wherein the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 17.08.2022 to 09.08.2022 by spending Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was earning his livelihood as an Agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month.

The accident in question due to the rash and negligent manner of driving of the said Canter bearing reg.No.KA-16-C-5792 by its driver and in the Jurisdictional Huliyurdurga police have registered a case in their crime No.132/2022, after investigation the said police have filed charge sheet against the said driver,
punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner constrained to file a petition and sought for awarding Rs.10,00,000/- as a compensation.
(SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.5888/2022 3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal and filed their respective written statement.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is that, the claim petition is lack of bonafides, benefit of merits, is speculative and requires to be dismissed in limine.
Further contended that, this respondent is not aware about the occupation, age of the petitioner.

Further contended that, at the time of accident, the respondent's vehicle was duly insured and the insurance policy was valid and its driver was having valid driving licence and he was not disqualified at the time of the accident to drive the said type of vehicle.
This respondent has not violated any terms and conditions of the policy issued by the Insurance company.
With these grounds the respondent No.1 sought for rejecting the claim petition.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is that, even though the brake system was in order (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.5888/2022 as per the IMV report, without a driving licence,
without competence to ride the said Honda Shine vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-06-EY-1138 rode the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner hit the insured vehicle Canter bearing reg.No.KA-16-C-5792 and caused the alleged accident.
Respondent further contended that, there is gross negligence on the part of the rider of the Honda Shine vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-06-EY-1138.
Respondent denied the occupation and earning of the petitioner, place, date and time of the accident.
Respondent admitted the issuance of policy in favour of Canter bearing reg.No.KA- 16-C-5792.
With these grounds the respondent No.2 sought for rejecting the claim petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 17.08.2022 at about 7.00 p.m., while he was riding his Honda Shine motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EY-1138 from Huliyurdurga towards Kenkere (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.5888/2022 Village on Maddur-Kunigal Main SH- 33 Road, at that time all of a sudden the driver of the Canter, bearing Reg.No.KA-16-C-5792 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the alleged RTA?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and Dr.Shailesh A V Rao has examined as PW.2 and in all got marked Ex.P.1 to 14.
On the other hand, respondents have not led their side evidence.

6. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.

3

7. My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
 (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.5888/2022  -:R E A S O N S:-
8. Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioner that, on 17.08.2022 at about 7.00 pm.,
when he was riding the Honda Sine vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-06-EY-1138 from Huliyurdurga towards Kenkere village on the extreme left side on Maduur - Kunigal main SH - 33 road slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations and when petitioner reached near Kodavatti junction, Huliyurdurga Bypass road,
Kunigal taluk, Tumkur, at that time

, suddenly, the driver of Canter bearing reg.No.KA-16- C-5792 came from Maddur towards Kunigal side in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations in a zig zag manner and dashed against his Honda Shine vehicle and caused the accident.
Due to said impact, he fell down along with the vehicle and sustained grevious injuries all over the body.
9. In order to prove the case, petitioner himself (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.5888/2022 examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief- examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition.
He also got marked Ex.P1 to P11.

The Aadhar card, FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, vehicle seizure panchanama, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, discharge summary, medical bills and prescriptions. medical prescriptions and bills.
10. I have perused Ex-P2 to Ex-P6 and 8.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 17.08.2022 at around 7.00 pm., and the FIR in crime No.0132/2022 came to be registered on 20.08.2022 at 16.00 at Huliyurdurga Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
Further the records reveal that, brother in law of petitioner has lodged the complaint on 20.08.2022 marked at Ex.P.3.
Ex . P.4
- spot panchanama reveals that accident occurred at Maddur - Kunigal road.
Ex . P.5

- vehicle seizure panchanam reveals spot of accident by direction as towards East - (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.5888/2022 Huliyurdurga police station premises beyond that, there is KSRTC bus station, towards West - Huliyurdurga police station premises beyond that, building of station, towards North and South - Huliyurdurga police station premises.

Ex. P.6 - IMV report reveals, the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defect of the motor vehicle and Chaluvaraju K.T vs Pathailingappa on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3267174/
4
Chargesheet marked at Ex.P.8 which has been filed against the driver of the Canter bearing reg.No.KA-16-C- 5792.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.
In his cross-examination he has specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that, due to his rash and negligent riding the accident has been occurred.
PW.1 denied the same.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.5888/2022 that the charge-sheet - Ex.P.8 filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of Canter bearing reg.No.KA-16-C- 5792 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:
In view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering, sustained by (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.5888/2022 the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
let me discuss one by one:

a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering: PW.1 has contended that due to the accident he sustained grievous injuries and during the course of treatment CT scan was done,
X-ray was taken which revealed polytrauma, traumatic brain injury with acute EDH with pneumocephalus with communited depressed fracture involving left parietal lobe, undisplaced head of left 2 nd proximal phalanx fracture and other grievous injuries all over the body.
In order to prove injuries caused to him, PW.1 has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 wherein doctor has opined injury is grievous as well as simple in nature.

The record shows that the petitioner took treatment in the hospital as an inpatient and he has (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.5888/2022 examined Dr.Shailesh A V Rao as PW.2 and he has assessed the disability of the petitioner.
Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.

Pw.1 contended that immediately after the accident he was shifted to Kunigal Government Hospital, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Bellur cross wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 17.08.2022 to 23.08.2022 for a period of 7 days.

Chaluvaraju K.T vs Pathailingappa on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3267174/
5 PW.1 has produced 19 medical bills marked at Ex.P.10 along with 16 medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.11.
On perusal of the Ex.P.10 which amounting to Rs.12,968/-.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not disputed regarding the medical bills and expenses (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.5888/2022 incurred by the petitioner towards treatment.
Hence, in all the Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.12,968/- is just and reasonable towards Medical expenses.
c) Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges:
Petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P.9.

On perusal of the same, Ex.P.9 is the discharge summary issued by Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Bellur cross wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 17.08.2022 to 23.08.2022 for a period of 7 days.
Therefore, during the time of treatment the petitioner also required healthy food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 7 days and also by including conveyance, a sum of Rs.10,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment,
conveyance and medical attendant charges.
(SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.5888/2022 d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:

PW.1 has contended that he was working as an Agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month.
But in this regard he has not produced any document.
In the absence of positive documents regarding petitioner's occupation and income this Tribunal will consider notional income.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2022 at 15,500/- p.m., Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2022 treated as Rs.15,500/- p.m.

Considering the age,
nature of injuries, treatment given & duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 3 months.
Thus, by taking into account the notional income of PW.1, this Tribunal awards Rs.46,500/- (15,500/- X 3) towards loss of income during treatment period.

e) Towards Loss of Income due to Disability: PW.1 (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.5888/2022 has examined Dr.Shailesh A V Rao as PW.2 and through him got marked OPD records marked at Ex.P.12 and neuro psychological assessment report marked at Ex.P.13 and mini mental state examination report marked at Ex.P.14, he has deposed that, on examination he was found that the petitioner sustained injury to his head and lost consciousness and he had lacerated wounds over his head, left forearm and left ankle.
He was disoriented, CT brain revealed left parietal acute extradural hemotoma with depressed fracture and pneumocephalus.
He also had fracture of left 2nd proximal phalanx, he was treated with medications.
He gradually improved and was discharged on 23.08.2022.

PW.2 further deposed that, on examination patient with slurred and stammering speech, he also has impaired memory and intelligence,
he has spastic left sided weakness with a power of 4 +/5.

Neuro psychological assessment was one on 08.06.2024 his IQ was 74, he is below average in thinking Chaluvaraju K.T vs Pathailingappa on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3267174/
6 and reasoning.

sentences.text: PW.2 has (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.5888/2022 assessed whole body disability at 20%.
By looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed whole body disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 15% whole body disability which cannot be ruled out.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 - Aadhar card in order to prove his age.
As per said document, he was born on 05.08.1996 and as on date of accident he was aged about 26 years.

Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 26 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "17" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
15,500 x 12 x 17 x 15% = Rs.4,74,300/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.4,74,300/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
f) Towards deprivation of Future Amenities:
 (SCCH-9) 18 MVC.No.5888/2022  PW.2 deposed that, while assessing, petitioner complains of pain in right leg and forearm difficulty to squat on floor, sit cross legged,
climb upstairs, walk on slope, kneel stand on affected limb, ablution lift weight over the head with right upper limb writing difficulty to do routine activities.
PW.2 further deposed that, there is a restriction of joint movement.
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
g) Towards future medical expenses: During cross examination, the doctor/PW.2 has not whispered about the future treatment to the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head future medical expenses.

12. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for (SCCH-9) 19 MVC.No.5888/2022 compensation as follows:

Total compensation .6,43,768/-
13.
Regarding Liability: Respondents have not led their side evidence and moreover, respondent No.2 has failed to disprove the negligence of the driver of the Canter bearing reg.No.KA-16-C-5792.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.5888/2022 to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2 being the Insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .6,43,768/- (Rupees six lakhs forty three thousand seven hundred sixty eight only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.5888/2022 insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 50% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 50% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification through e-payment.

Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
